title: Next-Gen Routing Engine
short: Re-architecting legacy HTTP router → achieved 10x throughput scaling.
challenge: The legacy HTTP router — inherited from the original monolith — bottlenecked at 5,000 requests per second. Profiling revealed that per-request memory allocation was the dominant cost: each request allocated ~1 KB across 7 heap objects, forcing the garbage collector into a tight loop that consumed 40% of CPU time under load.
solution: Implemented a trie-based router in Go utilizing sync.Pool to reuse memory buffers across requests. Route matching operates on the raw request byte slice with zero string allocations. Path parameters are extracted into stack-allocated buffers and only promoted to the heap when the handler explicitly requests them.
result: Throughput scales to 50,000+ requests per second on equivalent hardware. Per-request allocation dropped to 0 B/op. P99 latency reduced from 12ms to 0.8ms. The router now handles 100% of ScaleTech's edge traffic.

title: Vector Search Indexer
short: Custom implementation of HNSW indexing for sub-10ms similarity search at scale.
challenge: Existing vector search relied on a managed service with unpredictable latency spikes during index rebuilds. Query P99 exceeded 200ms under concurrent write load, breaking real-time recommendation SLAs.
solution: Built a custom HNSW indexer in Rust with memory-mapped segment files and incremental index updates. Write path batches embeddings into append-only segments; read path merges segment graphs lazily with copy-on-write semantics.
result: P99 query latency stabilized at 8ms under 10k QPS with concurrent writes. Index rebuild time reduced from 45 minutes to incremental updates under 2 seconds. Infrastructure cost dropped 60% versus managed alternative.
